body:
Codex pre-review (not a collaborator review; no marker) @ 3d268618bc18d2db91c470b5dbd1fa15031ef929

Verdict FINDINGS

- P1 — crates/app/src/geometry/import/mod.rs:142 (also :121): A valid hollow STL/OBJ has an outward outer shell and an inward cavity shell. The new normalization treats the cavity as an inverted solid and reverses it. A standalone probe using outer cube [0,10]^3 and inward inner cube [3,7]^3 reproduced this for both formats: inner signed volume -64 becomes +64, and total signed volume 936 becomes 1064. The import reports 12 facets corrected. This reverses valid cavity normals and swaps the concave/convex tests used by pencil and deburr. Preserve nesting-aware material orientation or refuse ambiguous nested shells. Existing step_orient_tests.rs::a_cavity_wound_inward_keeps_every_face documents the expected convention. No posted-program gouge was demonstrated.

Validation against upstream/main 4f4edcf35465c3ee83d7d4197685fc0e661e52f1: local merge clean. Both named import_outward pins pass. Quick gate GREEN, zero failures. camcraft-app clippy with all targets and -D warnings GREEN.

Mutations: streaming normalization removed -> STL pin RED (mesh equality fails). Buffered normalization removed -> STL and OBJ pins RED (outward-volume assertion fails). Both normalization calls restored byte-for-byte -> both pins GREEN. Worktree clean after restoration.

Rules: No new production unwrap/expect/panic. Changed source files are under 400 lines. No goldens, snapshot PNGs, PROCESS_VERSION, dependencies, .github or scripts changed. Body has Changelog: and Fixes #1672.

Fixed the P1 cavity-normal finding. STL and OBJ imports now refuse ambiguous inward shells whose bounds overlap another shell before normalization. This covers buffered imports and streaming STL loads. Isolated inward solids still turn outward.

Pinned by `nested_stl_cavity_is_refused_before_normalization` and `nested_obj_cavity_is_refused_before_normalization`. Both test buffered and disk imports using the review's hollow-cube fixture. Reverting the streaming call made the STL pin RED. Reverting the buffered call made both pins RED. Restoring both calls made all four import_outward tests GREEN.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is GREEN. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is GREEN.

New head: e93e5cbfbd23cc6298e735dad4487f56c33f37cd.

Please re-review this head. The PR remains a draft.

Codex pre-review (not a collaborator review; no marker) @ 3d268618bc18d2db91c470b5dbd1fa15031ef929

Verdict FINDINGS

- crates/app/src/geometry/import/mod.rs:142 (also :121): A valid hollow STL/OBJ with an outward 10 mm cube and an inward 6 mm cavity has its cavity shell flipped, reversing material-side normals used by pencil/deburr. Temporary tests for both formats fail: signed material volume changes from 784 to 1216 mm³ and the note reports 12 facets reversed. Distinguish nested void shells before flipping, or refuse ambiguous input. No posted gouge was demonstrated.

Tests: inward_stl_import_turns_outward_and_reports_it and inward_obj_import_turns_outward_and_reports_it PASS, including after restoration.
Gate: cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main GREEN, zero failures (44 s).
Clippy: cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings PASS.
Mutations: removing buffered normalization makes both pins RED. Removing streaming STL normalization makes its pin RED. Both calls restored; final pins GREEN; working tree clean.
AGENTS checks: changed source files below 400 lines; no added forbidden production unwrap/expect/panic; no changed goldens, snapshot PNGs, PROCESS_VERSION, dependencies, .github or scripts. Body includes Changelog: and Fixes #1672.
Local merge of upstream/main was already up to date. No push or label changes.

Codex pre-review (not a collaborator review; no marker) @ e93e5cbfbd23cc6298e735dad4487f56c33f37cd

Verdict CLEAN

Findings: none.

Trial merge with upstream/main 4f4edcf35465c3ee83d7d4197685fc0e661e52f1 was clean. All four import_outward pins passed, including after mutation restoration. Quick gate passed with CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 (app lib and 16 suites). The initial gate attempt failed before compilation because sccache could not read its server response. Clippy passed for camcraft-app, all targets, with warnings denied.

Mutations: disabling buffered normalization made both inward pins RED. Disabling streaming normalization made the STL inward pin RED. Bypassing overlap refusal made both nested pins RED. Removing the inward-body filter made an extra fixture RED. Removing the early-return optimization stayed GREEN; behavior is equivalent. All changes were restored.

Extra cases passed for STL and OBJ: an isolated inward cube beside an outward cube, also with two overlapping outward components. All resulting bodies had positive volume and correction notes appeared. Temporary tests were removed. No machine run or posted-program safety proof was attempted.

Changed files are under 400 lines. No new unwrap/expect/panic outside tests. No golden, snapshot PNG, PROCESS_VERSION, dependency, .github or scripts changes. The body includes Changelog: and Fixes #1672.

<!-- pr-reviewer: e93e5cbfbd23cc6298e735dad4487f56c33f37cd -->

Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.

What looks good:
- The fix closes the import gap that #1617 left for STL and OBJ. Both formats reuse the per-body orientation check.
- The buffered paths and the streaming STL path normalize alike. The tests cover both routes.
- The new refusal protects cavities. The code does not silently reverse an inward nested shell. It refuses by name, and the message says what to do.
- The decision file records the review correction and the conservative bounds rule.
- The note rides `Graded.notes` into the ImportModel command, so the status line shows it. No new field was needed.

Results, merged with main:
- Built and tested on the self-hosted runner, pr-test run 43635481311: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43635481311 . Head e93e5cbf trial-merged with main at 101d82f9. All steps green.
- Quick gate: 0 failed, 1 step. The `import_outward` suite ran 4 tests, all ok: `inward_stl_import_turns_outward_and_reports_it`, `inward_obj_import_turns_outward_and_reports_it`, `nested_stl_cavity_is_refused_before_normalization`, `nested_obj_cavity_is_refused_before_normalization`.
- The STEP import suites passed on the merged tree, `import_step_outward` and `import_step_guard` among them. The #1617 STEP normalization stays intact, and the #1638 module declarations were kept.
- App lib tests: 303 passed, 1 ignored.
- Clippy on camcraft-app, all targets, warnings denied: clean.
- Law checks passed: no unwrap, expect or panic outside tests; non-finite meshes are gated before the orientation code runs; the body index into the bounds vector is safe, because the winding pass numbers bodies before it fills that vector.

Requested before merge:
- None.

Questions / notes (not blocking):
- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/mesh_outward.rs` has no "Provenance:" line. Its sibling import modules carry one. One line would match the clean-room rule: the body verdict comes from `step_outward` (Zhang & Chen; Botsch et al.), and the bounds guard is our own choice from this review.
- The bounds guard also refuses two separate shells whose boxes touch face to face. That is conservative and recorded in the decision file. A later nesting classifier can narrow it.
- `mesh_outward.rs` indexes the bounds vector directly. `step_outward.rs` uses `get` for the same vector. Both are safe here. One style would read better.

Not exercised:
- No machine run and no posted-program safety proof. The pencil and deburr height trace is recorded on the issue.
- The gate ran on the macOS runner. This PR adds no OS-specific code, so no Windows re-run is owed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

- Gate route: pr-test.yml run 43635481311 on the macOS runner. The quick gate passed; clippy is clean.
